concurrency_note: saas_gate issues sequential, single deterministic HTTP exchanges (GET /, /health, /login) against a scripted fixture server; each probe's response is fixed for the scenario. There is no concurrent/racing dimension in the fixture target to evade — the rate-limit probe counts sequential attempts, not concurrent ones.

authority_boundary.proves: over a running HTTP endpoint, every FAIL-class SaaS NFR finding the gate makes fires on an injected instance (missing security header, a CSRF cookie whose SameSite is not Lax/Strict even when disguised with stray whitespace), while a documented non-FAIL boundary (a never-429 /login without --rate-limit-required, a header served via case-insensitive name indirection) correctly does NOT fire — driven end-to-end through the real CLI (real urllib.request, real HTTP, real header parsing)
authority_boundary.artifact: the REAL scripts/saas_gate.py CLI run as a subprocess against a scripted, deterministic local http.server on 127.0.0.1 (tests/fixtures/gate_validation/saas_gate_clean/saas_gate_server.py), with a trivial fixture repo (pyproject.toml -> detect_stack ['python']) as --repo
assumptions: VALIDATED AGAINST A SCRIPTED LOCAL HTTP FIXTURE SERVER, NOT A LIVE PRODUCTION/STAGING URL (CTR-fh-044): a real deployment's TLS configuration, load-balancer/proxy-injected headers, CDN or WAF behaviour, and rate-limiter timing may surface additional findings — or mask them — that this record says nothing about
the base URL is HTTP, so HSTS is a WARN (not a FAIL) and cookie Secure is not required; an HTTPS target changes those to FAIL-eligible and is out of this record's scope

tenant-isolation, performance/response-time, structured-logging (no --log-sample), and audit-trail checks are SKIPPED by run_gate without a live multi-user app / log sample and are therefore not exercised here — a SKIPPED status is honestly reported, never counted as a pass
the gate's verdict (report.ok) is FALSE iff any finding has status FAIL; WARN/SKIPPED/NA never block, by design

seeded_defect_trials.injected: an explicitly-supplied --base-url that cannot be reached. The target's actual security posture is unknown, not good; before #289 the six-check header/CSRF battery collapsed into one SKIPPED, and SKIPPED can never fail --gate.

scenario 'missing_headers': the root response omits Content-Security-Policy and X-Content-Type-Options entirely -> two FAIL findings (content-security-policy 'missing', x-content-type-options 'missing (want nosniff)')

scenario 'csrf_samesite_none_spaced': the session cookie carries 'SameSite = None' with stray whitespace a naive substring check might miss; the structural _cookie_attrs parser still normalizes it to samesite=none and FAILs the csrf check ('SameSite=none (need Lax/Strict)')

scenario 'headers_lowercased': an otherwise-healthy response serves every security header NAME lower-cased (content-security-policy, x-content-type-options, ...). The gate's case-insensitive _hget must still recognize them as present+healthy -> zero FAIL findings. A certified non-coverage-evasion boundary: casing indirection neither dodges detection nor causes a spurious finding, so the gate correctly does not fire.

scenario 'no_rate_limit': /login returns 200 on every one of the 20 probe attempts, never 429. Absent --rate-limit-required, check_rate_limit marks this WARN (not FAIL) by design -> report.ok stays True. A never-429 endpoint is a certified non-finding under the default scope, not a scanner miss, so the gate correctly does not fire.

validated_by: chief-wiggum#184; re-authored for chief-wiggum#295: chief_wiggum/hashing.py gained ID_BEARING_ARTIFACTS/find_id_bearing_artifacts/scan_malformed_ids (reusing trace_ids.near_miss_ids from #281 rather than a second detector). hashing.py is a finding-affecting scanner_version hash input for every shipped gate, so this gate's version moved even though its OWN behaviour is unchanged — trials and clean-corpus runs are unchanged and were re-verified live.; re-authored for chief-wiggum#289: a network failure on an explicitly-supplied --base-url collapsed the entire six-check header/CSRF battery into a single SKIPPED finding — and SKIPPED can never fail --gate, so an unreachable target passed the security battery by not being probed at all. A new ERROR status, distinct from the honest SKIPPED of an absent probe, is now emitted per check when the probe cannot run, and report.ok/--gate fail on ERROR exactly as on FAIL. --repo is validated (exit 2 for a nonexistent path) instead of silently degrading to an empty stack. to_dict carries a measured denominator (total/measured/skipped/error). The honest-absence path — no --base-url given at all — still reports SKIPPED and does NOT block; trials unchanged and re-verified live.; re-authored for chief-wiggum#370: saas_gate gained two security checks — `secret-hygiene`, which flags provisioned secret values carrying trailing whitespace, and `psk-callable`, which requires an internal endpoint to reject WITHOUT the secret AND succeed WITH it. The second is the point of the ticket: those are independent properties, and every existing check read '401 without a secret = pass', which an endpoint nobody can ever call satisfies perfectly. The real incident ran a production reconcile endpoint unreachable by every possible caller for a month because its Secret Manager value was created with `echo` and carried a trailing 0x0a; staging's copy happened to lack it, so tests and staging never surfaced it. Both new checks are ADDITIVE and default to SKIPPED when their inputs are absent (no --secrets-file, no --psk-path), so no existing finding class changed and no existing threshold moved; the clean-corpus security_checks denominator rises 7->9 because the gate now genuinely measures two more things, and that number is re-derived live by tests/test_saas_gate.py rather than restamped. The 5 seeded trials and the clean-corpus run are unchanged and were re-executed live. New guards mutation-tested. Re-authored again after adversarial review of the same change: the PSK probe accepted ANY status >= 400 as 'rejected without the secret', so a 500 or a 429 followed by a 200 with the secret read as a clean pass while the endpoint was crashing or throttling - the gate certifying authentication it never observed, which is the same shape as the defect it exists to catch. It now requires 401/403 and reports anything else as ERROR. Also: a TypeError raised inside the caller's getter was mislabelled 'http_get does not accept headers', and check_secret_hygiene crashed on str values. Still additive, still SKIPPED by default; trials and clean-corpus run re-executed live. Further hardened in the same review round: the probe pre-validates the secret for 0x0a/0x0d/0x00 and non-latin-1 BEFORE it reaches any HTTP client, because http.client.putheader raises with the header value embedded and the generic handler would have interpolated the secret into a finding that reaches stdout and the JSON report - the one input this check exists for would have leaked it. Exception text is additionally scrubbed of the secret. An explicitly requested --psk-path without --psk-secret-env or without --base-url is now a usage error rather than a SKIPPED finding that cannot fail --gate, and a --secrets-file with non-string values is refused rather than coerced into plausible secrets that pass hygiene.
